html:
The Iraq War began on 20 March 2003 when the United States, Britain and allies invaded Iraq to overthrow Saddam Hussein, claiming he held weapons of mass destruction. None were found. Baghdad fell on 9 April.

The occupation dissolved the army and the Ba'ath Party, and an insurgency grew. Sunni militants, including al-Qaeda in Iraq, and Shia militias fought a sectarian war that peaked in 2006 and 2007. Saddam was hanged in 2006. A surge of American troops and a Sunni tribal revolt against al-Qaeda brought violence down.

American troops left in December 2011. Hundreds of thousands of Iraqis died by most estimates. The remnants of al-Qaeda in Iraq became the Islamic State, which took Mosul in 2014 (ISIS declares a caliphate). See also the Gulf War.
sum: The Iraq War began on 20 March 2003 when the United States, Britain and allies invaded Iraq to overthrow Saddam Hussein, claiming he held weapons of mass destruction. None were found. Baghdad fell on 9 April.
